item.title: AI Builders Fellowship 2026 (Internet Archive Canada x BC + AI)
item.description:
Organisation: Internet Archive Canada (IAC) in partnership with BC + AI

Location: Remote, open to builders anywhere in the world. Optional in-person showcase at Futureproof Festival in Vancouver, Canada on 28 October 2026 if the project is ready.

Award: $5,000 award for one selected builder. No application fee.

Duration: Six-week build, 1 September to mid-October 2026, remote, with support from BC + AI throughout

Deadline: Closed 21 Aug 2026

A $5,000 fellowship to spend six weeks turning a very large Canadian public archive into something new. THE MATERIAL: Internet Archive Canada's Government Publications collection, part of the Democracy's Library project, holding over 104,000 text items, roughly 22.1 million scanned pages and about 48.25 TB of Canadian public-record material, browsable at archive.org/details/governmentpublications. WHAT TO BUILD: deliberately open-ended. The call names a search tool that answers a real question with page-level citations, a timeline tracing one policy across decades of government language, and a sonic or visual piece built from archival material, but explicitly invites work nobody has thought of yet. The requirements are that it is useful, that it is imaginative, and that the code is open source when it is done. ORIGIN: the fellowship came out of conversations between BC + AI's Kris Kruger and IAC executive director Andrea Mills about treating a public archive as material for new work rather than only something to preserve. IAC brings the archive, BC + AI brings a community of builders used to working in public. ELIGIBILITY: anyone, anywhere in the world; one builder is selected. APPLICATION: a specific project description grounded in the collection, a phase-by-phase work plan for the six weeks, and a success metric, submitted at bc-ai.ca/fellowship/apply. KEY DATES: applications close 21 August 2026 at 11:59pm Pacific; fellow selected by 31 August; build runs 1 September to mid-October; showcase at Futureproof Festival in Vancouver on 28 October 2026 if the project is ready.

item.title: Helpmann Fellowships 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Helpmann Academy

Location: South Australia (applicant must be a current South Australian resident); funded activity may take place anywhere.

Award: Up to AUD 7,500 per fellowship, three fellowships available. Supported by the James & Diana Ramsay Foundation. No application fee.

Duration: Funded activity must occur between 1 January 2027 and 31 December 2027

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

Three Helpmann Fellowships of up to AUD 7,500 support ambitious, self-directed projects that advance the artistic and professional development of emerging creatives. Fellowships are open across all eligible disciplines, to individuals and to collectives, and funding can go to larger-scale creative projects, tailored professional development, or a combination of both. Previous fellowships have supported the creation of new work, exhibitions and performances, residencies and internships, touring and recording, specialised training, and long-term professional development; each fellowship is shaped by the recipient rather than a fixed programme. ELIGIBILITY IS NARROW AND GEOGRAPHIC: applicants must be current residents of South Australia and either final-year students or graduates within five years of a supported degree at Adelaide University, the University of Adelaide, Flinders University, or the University of South Australia. Honours students and graduates (up to five years after the final year of study) are eligible where honours was undertaken directly following the undergraduate degree. Masters and PhD candidates and graduates are not eligible unless they qualify through their undergraduate or honours study. Final-year students may apply provided the funded activity takes place after studies are completed and within the activity timeframe. Applications are assessed on artistic merit, alignment with career development, feasibility, commitment to learning, and level of ambition. The online application requires a CV (max two pages), an official academic transcript, a budget on the Helpmann template, a timeline, project confirmations, letters of support from an academic and an industry referee, and four to six images or one to two audio-visual work samples. An online information session runs 4 August 2026 at 6pm ACST, and the Program Manager, Toni Wills, takes online or in-person application chats (info@helpmannacademy.com.au). Applications opened 15 July 2026 and close 31 August 2026 at 11:59pm ACST, for activity occurring 1 January to 31 December 2027. Free to apply.

item.title: Beinecke Library Short-Term Research Fellowships 2027-2028 (Yale)
item.description:
Organisation: Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library, Yale University

Location: Onsite at Yale Library Special Collections, New Haven, Connecticut, USA. Open to academic and independent scholars locally and globally, regardless of institutional association.

Award: USD 5,000 per month for research visits between two weeks and two months. Funding is paid at the beginning of the fellowship where possible (payment to international fellows often takes several weeks); fellows are responsible for taxes on the award. Free to apply.

Duration: Two weeks to two months of onsite research, conducted between 1 July 2027 and 30 June 2028; awards cannot be deferred

Deadline: Closed 15 Aug 2026

The Beinecke Library Fellowship Program offers competitive short-term fellowships to support research projects that substantively engage with Yale Library Special Collections materials. WHO CAN APPLY: academic and independent scholars, locally and globally, with or without an institutional affiliation; the library explicitly welcomes applicants regardless of institutional association, race, cultural background, ability, sexual orientation, gender or socioeconomic status. Applications using traditional archival and bibliographic research methods are encouraged, and so are creative, interdisciplinary and non-traditional approaches to working with the collections, which makes this a live option for artists and writers whose practice is research-driven. WHAT YOU GET: USD 5,000 per month for an onsite research visit of between two weeks and two months, paid at the start of the fellowship whenever possible (international fellows should expect payment to take several weeks); fellows pay their own taxes on the award. TIMELINE: applications for the 2027-2028 awards opened 1 June 2026 and close 15 August 2026, via Interfolio; all decisions are notified by 31 January 2027; research must be conducted between 1 July 2027 and 30 June 2028, and awards cannot be deferred.

item.title: Queens Museum: QM-Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Emerging Artists 2027-2028
item.description:
Organisation: Queens Museum (with the Jerome Foundation)

Location: Queens, New York City, USA

Award: $20,000 fellowship award per artist (two artists selected), plus professional development consultations, mentorship from Queens Museum staff and an established New York-based artist, and a solo exhibition at the Queens Museum in 2028. No application fee.

Duration: One-year fellowship (2027-2028), culminating in a 2028 solo exhibition

Deadline: 28 Sep 2026

The QM-Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Emerging Artists selects two emerging visual artists living in New York City for its 2027-2028 cohort. Each fellow receives a $20,000 award, professional development consultations, mentorship from Queens Museum staff and an established New York-based artist, and a solo exhibition at the Queens Museum in 2028, with curatorial support across a full year of project development. Aimed at early-career visual artists (roughly two to ten years of professional practice) who have a consistent practice and developing public profile but have not yet reached major institutional recognition. ELIGIBILITY: must currently reside in one of NYC's five boroughs and maintain residency through the fellowship; artists enrolled in degree-granting programs are not eligible; review the detailed criteria on exhibition history, previous grants and years of practice. Supported by the Jerome Foundation. Apply via the Queens Museum fellowship program page. Deadline: 28 September 2026, 11:59 PM EST.

item.title: Instituto Sacatar: Sacatar Fellowship 2027 (Bahia, Brazil)
item.description:
Organisation: Instituto Sacatar

Location: Itaparica island, Bahia, Brazil. Open to all nationalities.

Award: Fully hosted residency: private bedroom with attached bathroom, three meals a day (except Saturday evenings, Sundays and Brazilian holidays), an individual studio suited to the discipline, weekly laundry, logistical support and airport transfer from Salvador. NO STIPEND, no airfare and no materials budget. USD 25 application fee. One French artist may additionally receive airfare and a stipend through Villa Fatumbi.

Duration: Approximately eight weeks; specific session dates are listed in the application.

Deadline: 28 Aug 2026

Brazil's longest-running artist residency, on the island of Itaparica across the bay from Salvador, hosting six to eight artists per session for roughly eight weeks. Open to all creative disciplines and, unusually for this region, to all nationalities, which makes it one of the few genuinely international residencies in Latin America. Sacatar provides full hosting (private room, three meals daily, individual studio, laundry, local logistics and connections) but explicitly does NOT provide a stipend, airfare to Salvador, art materials or discretionary local expenses, so applicants must fund their own travel. Individual artists only; group proposals are not accepted and former Sacatar Fellows may not reapply. COVID vaccination is required. NOTE: there is a USD 25 application fee. Apply through SlideRoom by 28 August 2026. Contact info@sacatar.org.

Open call details

item.title: Stiftung Künstler*dorf Schöppingen: Residency Fellowship 2027 Open Call
item.description:
Organisation: Stiftung Künstler*dorf Schöppingen

Location: Schöppingen, Germany (residency requires living and working on-site)

Award: Stipend of EUR 1,500 per month, minus roughly EUR 100-200 for rent and operating expenses. For collectives, EUR 1,000 per person up to a maximum of EUR 3,000 per month, minus rent and operating costs. Travel, insurance and material costs are covered only in exceptional cases, on request.

Duration: Residency of two to six months during 2027; period chosen by agreement and availability

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

Stiftung Künstler*dorf Schöppingen offers residency fellowships for professional visual artists, authors and composers; since 2023 applications from collectives are also accepted. The call is open to people of all nationalities and ages, and accommodation for partners, family members or assistance can be arranged upon agreement and availability (for physical, cognitive or sensory disabilities, contact the foundation to explain any barriers). Fellows reside and work at the Künstler*dorf for a period of their choosing between two and six months, using the premises and infrastructure on-site. The stipend is EUR 1,500 per month, minus roughly EUR 100-200 for rent and operating expenses; for collectives it is EUR 1,000 per person up to a maximum of EUR 3,000 per month, minus rent and operating costs. Travel, insurance or material costs are covered only in exceptional cases on request. The fellowship is not designed as a production residency and there is no obligation to present results, though exhibition and presentation facilities are available and the voluntary co-organization of events (lectures, readings, workshops or similar) is welcomed. A willingness to participate in events and to engage in exchange with other fellows is a prerequisite. Selection is made by expert juries on the quality of previous work, the quality and plausibility of the project for Schöppingen, and program contributions (interaction / community building). Applications for 2027 can be submitted from 27 June to 31 August 2026 (midnight CET) via the online application portal.

item.title: Accent Sisters Work-Study Fellowship Program 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Accent Sisters

Location: 89 5th Ave, Suite 702, New York, NY 10003 (hybrid; part-time, 3 days/week, on-site work required)

Award: Stipend of USD 600 (paid in two installments), plus free passes to all in-person events and classes, fellow discounts, and one-on-one mentorship.

Duration: 20 August to 20 December 2026; part-time, 3 days per week

Deadline: Closed 01 Aug 2026

Accent Sisters offers a work-study fellowship for individuals passionate about literature, visual arts, and community engagement. The fellowship provides hands-on experience in a bookstore and a hybrid event space where exhibitions, book launches, film screenings, educational programs, and other public programming take place. It is ideal for someone looking to build a career in cultural institutions, independent bookstores, or art galleries. Fellows work closely with both the bookstore and gallery teams, gaining skills in book curation, exhibit planning, marketing, and community outreach, while developing a personal project that merges these disciplines. WHAT YOU GET: opportunities to work with writers, artists, and creators; a chance to pitch projects, events, and programs for a diverse community; free passes to all in-person events and classes; fellow discounts; a showcase of your personal project toward the end of the fellowship; one-on-one mentorship with the Accent team; and a USD 600 stipend. Open to upcoming seniors, upcoming second-year graduate students, and recent graduates of undergraduate/graduate programs. Four tracks are offered and applicants generally choose one: Program Coordination & Community Engagement; Curation & Administration; Graphic Design & Digital Asset Management; or Marketing & Business Development. The fellowship runs 20 August to 20 December 2026 (part-time, 3 days per week, on-site required). Applications are reviewed from 15 July to 1 August 2026.

item.title: The Hodder Fellowship 2027-2028 (Princeton University)
item.description:
Organisation: Princeton University, Lewis Center for the Arts

Location: Princeton, New Jersey, USA; academic-year appointment as a Visiting Fellow (no U.S. citizenship required)

Award: USD 93,000 stipend for the 10-month appointment as a Visiting Fellow. No formal teaching is involved. No application fee.

Duration: One academic year (10-month appointment), 2027-2028

Deadline: 08 Sep 2026

The Hodder Fellowship is given to artists and writers of exceptional promise to pursue independent projects at Princeton University during the academic year. Potential Hodder Fellows are composers, choreographers, performance artists, visual artists, writers, translators, or other kinds of artists or humanists who have 'much more than ordinary intellectual and literary gifts'; they are selected more 'for promise than for performance.' Given the strength of the applicant pool, most successful Fellows have published a first book or have similar achievements in their own fields; the Hodder is designed to provide Fellows with the 'studious leisure' to undertake significant new work. Fellows spend an academic year at Princeton with no formal teaching, supported by a USD 93,000 stipend for the 10-month Visiting Fellow appointment. IMPORTANT: for this cycle, applications are accepted only for the Program in Dance, the Program in Theater and Music Theater, the Program in Visual Arts, and the Department of Music. Fellowships are not intended to fund work leading to an advanced degree; one need not be a U.S. citizen to apply; previous recipients of the Princeton Arts Fellowship are not eligible. To apply, submit a resume, a 500-word project proposal, and samples of your work (writing sample, images, video links to performances, etc.). Applicants may apply for the Hodder Fellowship only twice in a lifetime. Applications are submitted via Interfolio. The application cycle closes 8 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EDT.

Open call details

item.title: Adrianna Newell Fellowship at Arts&Rec 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Arts&Rec Inc

Location: Stamford, NY (Western Catskills), USA

Award: Live/work residency: use of a 1000 sq ft studio and attached apartment, plus a $1,500 total materials stipend and per diem. Travel (especially international) is not funded. No application fee.

Duration: October 2026 (four weeks to two months, based on project needs; possible extension into November)

Deadline: Closed 31 Jul 2026

Inaugural Adrianna Newell Fellowship, a live/work studio residency in Stamford, NY (Western Catskills) for October 2026, with possible extension into November. Named for board member Adrianna Newell, it invites queer lens-based artists working in photography and moving image with an active, research-driven or conceptually rich practice, especially work engaging queer perspectives on land, rurality and regional space, or queer identity, memory, intimacy, community and embodiment. Open to artists from everywhere. Fellows receive a 1000 sq ft studio with attached apartment, a $1,500 combined materials stipend and per diem, and introductions to the local creative community; an open-studio presentation, artist talk or public exhibition at the end is required. Travel, especially international, is not funded (residents are encouraged to seek travel support elsewhere). Apply by emailing a single PDF (one-page description of your work and planned project, 10 to 20 work samples with short descriptions, and a current CV) to programs@artsrec.org. Deadline: 31 July 2026; notices by end of August.

item.title: Wave Hill / AnkhLave Arts Alliance: 2027 Van Lier Fellowship (NYC)
item.description:
Organisation: Wave Hill / AnkhLave Arts Alliance

Location: Wave Hill Public Garden and Cultural Center, the Bronx, New York City, USA. For NYC-based BIPOC visual artists aged 30 or younger.

Award: $10,435 stipend, including an $8,000 honorarium, a transportation stipend for the residency, and professional development opportunities, plus the Winter Workspace residency, a solo exhibition with public programs, mentorship from Wave Hill curatorial staff and arts professionals, and AnkhLave Alumni Network benefits. Two fellowships awarded. No application fee.

Duration: January to December 2027; Winter Workspace residency 23 February - 18 April 2027; solo exhibition 15 May - 4 July 2027

Deadline: Closed 10 Aug 2026

Wave Hill, in partnership with AnkhLave Arts Alliance, invites NYC-based artists who identify as BIPOC to apply for the 2027 Van Lier Fellowship as part of the 9th Annual AnkhLave Garden Project at Wave Hill Public Garden and Cultural Center in the Bronx. The project supports artists who draw on research, scholarship and lived knowledge to present site-responsive work at the intersection of nature, culture and place, engaging with Wave Hill's plant collections, history, design and architecture. The Van Lier Fellowship (funded by the Edward and Sally Van Lier Fund through the New York Community Trust) will be awarded to two NYC-based visual artists aged 30 or younger. FELLOWSHIP: participation in the Winter Workspace residency (23 February - 18 April 2027); a $10,435 stipend including an $8,000 honorarium and transportation stipend; a solo exhibition in the Sunroom or Sun Porch (15 May - 4 July 2027); public engagement through Winter Workspace programming and a Meet the Artist program; mentorship with Wave Hill curatorial staff, working artists and arts professionals; and AnkhLave Alumni Network benefits. ELIGIBILITY: emerging artists 30 or younger (born 1997 or after) from historically underrepresented communities; live in one of the five NYC boroughs; demonstrate financial need; have completed college and not be enrolled in a degree-granting program during the residency; not represented by a commercial gallery; available for both programs; cannot have been a Van Lier Fellow elsewhere or have previously done a Winter Workspace residency or exhibited at Wave Hill or with AnkhLave. Works may not include nudity, depictions of violence or profanity. Artists may apply to only one of the two 2027 AnkhLave Garden Project opportunities. Questions: visualarts@wavehill.org with '2027 Van Lier-Ankhlave' in the subject. DEADLINE: 10 August 2026. Apply via SlideRoom.

Open call details

item.title: JCAL: ARTWorks Fellowship 2026-2027
item.description:
Organisation: Jamaica Center for Arts and Learning (JCAL)

Location: Jamaica, Queens, New York City, USA. Open to visual artists based in New York City (preferably Queens) or Long Island; priority to Queens-based BIIPOC artists.

Award: $5,000 per Fellow, paid out over the course of the program, plus free shared studio space at JCAL (about 550 sq ft, as available), a 7 x 4 ft storage closet, one free JCAL class (space-available), an Artist Mentor and seminar series, and a concluding two-month group exhibition with catalogue in JCAL's Miller and Community galleries. No application fee.

Duration: Six-month fellowship: 7 October 2026 to 18 June 2027; exhibition opens 9 April 2027

Deadline: Closed 13 Jul 2026

Jamaica Center for Arts and Learning (JCAL) invites New York City-based visual artists to apply for ARTWorks, its Artist Fellowship Training Seminar Series: a six-month fellowship focused on career sustainability that amplifies the work of emerging, underrepresented visual artists. Six Fellows treat their practice as a small business, set entrepreneurial and professional goals, and build a long-term plan, supported by a Program Manager, an established Artist Mentor, cohort meetings, and at least six seminar events (past topics: copyright and contracts, working with galleries and collectors, grant writing, taxes and accounting, marketing, art handling). SUPPORT: $5,000 per Fellow paid over the program, free shared studio space (about 550 sq ft, as available) with a storage closet, one free JCAL class, and a concluding two-month group exhibition with catalogue (opens 9 April 2027). ELIGIBILITY: reside in New York City (preferably Queens) or Long Island; identify as BIIPOC (Black, Immigrant, Indigenous, People of Color); demonstrate clarity of concept and strong craft with a deep commitment to social practice; must NOT have received major exposure via exhibitions, grants or residencies; must not be enrolled in any college degree or certificate program; past Fellows ineligible. Priority to Queens-based artists of underrepresented communities; multidisciplinary practices welcome, but the program focuses on visual artists working in traditional forms. APPLY via Submittable with six images OR two 3-5 minute videos, a one-page work-sample description, artist statement (max 300 words), one professional reference (max 300 words), CV, and a paragraph on your expectations of ARTWorks. Jury reviews submissions without obvious identifiers. TIMELINE: first-round notifications 3 August 2026, interviews 11-14 August, Fellows notified 21 August, program runs 7 October 2026 to 18 June 2027. DEADLINE: midnight Monday 13 July 2026 (portal closes 14 July 2026, 6:00 AM ET).

Open call details

item.title: Target Margin Theater: TMT Institute Fellowship 2026-27
item.description:
Organisation: Target Margin Theater

Location: Brooklyn, New York, United States (Sunset Park). Fellows must be available in person for intensives, monthly breakfasts, and excursions.

Award: USD 2,000 stipend, plus space, material resources, and collaborators to support each Fellow's experiments. No application fee.

Duration: 2026-27 season: three intensive sessions in Brooklyn (5-8 November 2026, 8-10 January 2027, 19-21 March 2027), monthly breakfasts October 2026 through May 2027, and an Open Studio weekend in June 2027.

Deadline: Closed 22 Jul 2026

Target Margin Theater invites applications for its next cohort of TMT Institute Fellows for the 2026/2027 season. The Institute is a cohort of artists who seek to radically disrupt and re-examine their existing practice without any goal or expected result: pure experimentation with no product-oriented end goal. Fellows pursue no project, no developmental stage, no deliverable; misfires, dead ends, and bad ideas are considered a fruitful part of the work. SUPPORT: TMT provides space, material resources, collaborators, and a USD 2,000 stipend. STRUCTURE: three short intensive sessions at Target Margin Theater in Brooklyn (5-8 November 2026, 8-10 January 2027, and 19-21 March 2027, all day with some evening hours), monthly breakfasts at Junior's in Brooklyn (20 October, 30 November, 4 January, 1 February, 8 March, 5 April, 3 May), and occasional excursions. After the second intensive, each Fellow commits to an exploration pursued outside group gatherings, supported by TMT resources. The season ends with an Open Studio weekend in June 2027 to share explorations with the community; this is not a performance and should not be an audience-attended, time-bounded show. WHO CAN APPLY: artists from any discipline within or outside theater, as well as production, technical, and administrative workers in the arts. Applicants must have an established, existing body of work and practice they are committed to changing; do not apply with a project. Recent graduates of training programs are unlikely to be appropriate candidates; no formal education level or degree is required. SELECTION: TMT staff and artistic community review applications and invite a handful of candidates to interview; all applicants are notified by October. Deadline: Wednesday 22 July 2026, 11:59 pm EST.

Open call details

item.title: Ucross Fellowship for Native American Visual Artists: Spring 2027
item.description:
Organisation: Ucross Foundation

Location: Sheridan, Wyoming, USA

Award: Fully funded fellowship residency; living accommodations, meals, and work space provided. No application fee.

Duration: Spring session (February through early June 2027); residencies range from two to six weeks

Deadline: Closed 15 Jul 2026

The Ucross Fellowship for Native American Visual Artists is a dedicated fellowship within Ucross Foundation's residency program, offering fully funded time and space to make work on a working cattle ranch in the foothills of Wyoming's Bighorn Mountains. The fellowship provides living accommodations, meals, and work space at no charge, with no application fee. One Fellowship winner is selected per session; all applicants also have the option of being considered for a general Ucross residency. ELIGIBILITY: open to Native American visual artists who are practicing contemporary artists currently producing work in any visual medium, including but not limited to painting, drawing, mixed media, sculpture, printmaking, photography, video, animation, performance art, installation, and ceramics; and who are enrolled members of a state-recognized or federally-recognized Tribe, Pueblo, Nation, Native Community, Political Entity, or Alaskan Native Village. The work sample and project description are the most significant features of the application. Unless the work is interdisciplinary, applicants are encouraged to apply in a single primary discipline and submit a work sample and project description emphasizing that discipline. Work-sample requirements: VISUAL ARTWORK, submit 10 images (JPEG format, no PDFs) with file names including title and size, plus a data sheet listing title, medium, size, and year of completion for each image; FILM/VIDEO/ANIMATION/PERFORMANCE, submit up to 3 video files (each under 8 minutes and smaller than 200 MB) or up to 3 Vimeo or YouTube links. The open call for the Spring 2027 session closes July 15, 2026 (apply by 11:59 p.m. MT). A separate Ucross Fellowship for Native American Writers is also offered.

item.title: Kala Fellowship Program
item.description:
Organisation: Kala Art Institute

Location: Berkeley, California, USA

Award: USD 3,000 stipend, 24/7 facility access for 1 to 9 months, 1 month of housing for artists outside the 9 Bay Area counties, a Kala class or workshop, and a group exhibition USD 25 application fee (free if applying December through January 15)

Duration: 1 to 9 months within the July 2026 to June 2027 fellowship period

Deadline: 01 Mar 2027

The Kala Fellowship Program supports international, national, and local artists producing innovative work in and across multiple media, with an emphasis on Kala's specialized printmaking, photography, and digital media equipment. The institute supports up to 6 artists per cycle with a USD 3,000 stipend, 24/7 access to its Berkeley facilities for 1 to 9 months, one month of housing for artists based outside the 9 Bay Area counties, a Kala class or workshop, and a culminating group show in the Kala Gallery. Applications are submitted through kala.slideroom.com and require a statement of interest, an artist CV, documentation of 5 to 10 recent works, and two references. Artists enrolled in a degree-granting program during the fellowship period are not eligible. The application opens in December with no fee through January 15, after which a USD 25 application fee applies through the March 1 deadline.

item.title: The Studios at MASS MoCA Residencies
item.description:
Organisation: MASS MoCA (Massachusetts Museum of Contemporary Art)

Location: North Adams, Massachusetts, USA

Award: Provides private 24/7 studio space, furnished housing, and seven communal meals per week. Financial aid is available so artists requesting it typically pay between USD 0 and USD 450 per week, and fully funded fellowships cover all residency fees for up to four weeks. Artists who fully self-fund pay a subsidized rate of USD 650 per week.

Duration: 2 or 4 weeks

Deadline: 01 Nov 2026

The Studios at MASS MoCA is a year-round residency program on the museum's campus in North Adams, Massachusetts, hosting up to 10 artists at a time for stays of two or four weeks. It primarily welcomes visual artists across all media and writers in all literary disciplines, and applicants from around the world are encouraged to apply. Residents receive 24-hour access to a private furnished studio, lodging in nearby apartments, and several communal meals each week, plus museum membership benefits and access to The Clark Art Institute. The program offers need-based financial aid (artists typically pay between USD 0 and USD 450 per week) and fully funded fellowships that cover all residency fees for up to four weeks. General application deadlines fall on May 1 and November 1 each year, and the application is free to submit.

item.title: Artivism & Amplifiers Fellowship 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Human Impacts Institute

Location: Global; pairs young climate leaders from the Global North and Global South. Open to speakers of English, Spanish, French, and Portuguese.

Award: USD 1,000 stipend upon completion. Supported by expert workshops and creative mentors.

Duration: Six-month program.

Deadline: Closed 01 Jul 2026

The Artivism & Amplifiers (A&A) Fellowship pairs young climate leaders from the Global North and Global South to co-create multimedia campaigns, exhibits, and installations for the Creative Climate Awards 2027. Over six months, fellows build skills in intercultural collaboration, climate storytelling, and community engagement, supported by expert workshops and creative mentors. The program is open to speakers of English, Spanish, French, and Portuguese. Fellows receive a USD 1,000 stipend upon completion. The organizers strongly encourage applications from people most impacted by the climate crisis, including those from the global majority, Indigenous, LGBTQIA+, immigrant, and diaspora communities, and people with disabilities. Applications close Wednesday 1 July 2026 at 9am GMT+2.

item.title: Springboard for the Arts: Rural Regenerator Fellowship 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Springboard for the Arts

Location: Upper Midwest, USA (rural communities). In-person retreat and Rural Futures Summit

Award: USD 15,000 unrestricted award per Fellow, plus one in-person retreat, USD 3,000 to support travel for Fellow Exchanges, and the opportunity to attend and present at Springboard's Rural Futures Summit. Six Fellows selected. No application fee mentioned.

Duration: 18-month fellowship

Deadline: Closed 18 Jun 2026

The Rural Regenerator Fellowship is an 18-month fellowship that brings together rural artists, creatives, and culture bearers to deepen their relationships, grow their work, and support rural exchange and solidarity across the Upper Midwest. Since 2021, Springboard for the Arts has invested more than USD 1 million in rural cultural organizers across the Upper Midwest, building a lasting network of support, solidarity, and exchange; 44 Fellows have come together to support each other's work and share ideas. The fellowship brings rural artists into a supportive peer network, helping to sustain and deepen their existing work while cultivating geographic exchange, mutual support, and solidarity across the rural Midwest. CURRENT CYCLE - Organizing for Care, Safety, and Solidarity: this cycle supports artists who are organizing their rural places for care, safety, and solidarity. Six rural artists, creatives, and culture bearers will each receive an unrestricted award of USD 15,000, one in-person retreat, USD 3,000 to support travel for Fellow Exchanges, and the opportunity to attend and present at Springboard's Rural Futures Summit. Peers, collaborators, and supporters may nominate a rural artist, though nomination is not required to apply and all applications are reviewed equally (the selection committee does not know whether an applicant was nominated). Deadline to apply: 18 June 2026.

item.title: Lighthouse Works: Fellowship Program 2027 (Fishers Island)
item.description:
Organisation: Lighthouse Works

Location: Fishers Island, New York, USA (in-person residency)

Award: Six-week fellowship providing housing, food, private studio space, and USD 1,750 in financial support. No application fee mentioned.

Duration: 6 weeks; fellowships occur year-round across five sessions

Deadline: 15 Oct 2026

Lighthouse Works' Fellowship Program supports a diverse range of cultural producers working at the vanguard of their creative fields. Fellowships are six weeks in length, occur year-round, and provide fellows with housing, food, studio space, and USD 1,750 in financial support. Fellows enjoy a private bedroom and share a kitchen, bathrooms, and living space in a 3-story Victorian house; all dietary needs are accommodated, and on most nights Lighthouse Works staff cook for and eat dinner with the fellows. Studios are located about 1.5 miles (a 30-minute walk) from the fellowship house, are private and flooded with light, and face the ocean adjacent to Silver Eel Cove where the island ferry arrives. Lighthouse Works also maintains a wood and metal fabrication shop and a kiln. While in residence, a fellow's primary obligation is to pursue their own work, though every fellow participates in two events, an Artist Talk and Open Studio, that bookend the fellowship; the program's intimate size allows for conversation, critique, and collaboration. Artistic excellence is the primary criterion for acceptance. Artists at any stage of their career are encouraged to apply through the online Slideroom system. SELECTION: staff review applications for completeness, a jury of experts in each artist's field reviews complete applications and identifies finalists, interviews are scheduled in early January, and applicants are notified in mid-January. The program is supported in part by a grant from the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation. APPLICATION CALL: Lighthouse Works accepts applications each year from September to October (the 2026 portal was open 15 September to 15 October 2025). The deadline shown here is the anticipated close of the next annual call for the 2027 cycle; confirm exact dates on the Lighthouse Works site when the portal reopens. Apply at http://thelighthouseworks.slideroom.com.

item.title: ARCAthens: Athens Residency Fellowships (Fall 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: ARCAthens

Location: Athens, Greece (in-person residency). Open to applicants not residing in Greece

Award: Fully funded: USD 3,000 Fellowship Prize, USD 200/week stipend toward food and local transport, basic coach round-trip airfare reimbursed, private bedroom and bathroom with shared kitchen, and studio access for Visual Art Fellows. No application fee.

Duration: 3 months, 10 September to 30 November 2026

Deadline: Closed 30 Jun 2026

The Athens Residency is the flagship program of ARCAthens, a not-for-profit founded in 2017, offering two fully-funded Fellowships (Visual Art and Curatorial) that enable artists, curators, and scholars to live and work in Athens, Greece, and respond to the city's ongoing cultural renaissance. The residency is a structured, research-driven program built around scheduled engagements with artists, curators, institutions, and collections, including arranged studio and private collection visits, guided institutional access, and select community events. Distinct from studio-isolated models, it emphasizes engagement and exchange, balancing focused visits with time for independent exploration. ELIGIBILITY: ARCAthens welcomes applicants from all countries and nationalities representing a broad range of creative thought and practice; the program is open to applicants not residing in Greece. PRACTICAL: 3-month duration; USD 3,000 Fellowship Prize; USD 200 per week stipend toward food and local transportation; a basic coach round-trip ticket is provided (Fellows purchase following ARCAthens approval of itinerary and cost, reimbursed within five business days; in cases of financial hardship ARCAthens may arrange travel directly). Fellows are responsible for all other expenses, including food, local transportation, and any production, installation, or shipping costs. Visas are not necessary for US nationals for the duration of the program; others are responsible for procuring visas as applicable. Facilities include a private bedroom and bathroom with shared kitchen; Visual Art Fellows have studio access. Two Fellows are in residence at one time. Working language is English. Selection is by a 3-person independent committee of arts professionals. No fee, open call. TIMELINE: application deadline 30 June 2026 (closes 11:00 p.m. ET); notification of Fellowships mid July; residency 10 September to 30 November 2026.
